description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:416-423 — verify_embedded_scts() runs each SCT through verify_sct_for_precert() inside an is_ok() check. Per-SCT failures (InvalidSignature, UnknownLog, SctTimestampOutsideLogWindow, UnsupportedSignatureAlgorithm, UnsupportedVersion) correctly fold into 0-count. But verify_sct_for_precert() also returns Error::ParseError when issuer_cert_der cannot be parsed and Error::CertDerTooLong when leaf TBS exceeds 2^24-1 — these are programmer/input errors, not per-SCT trust outcomes, yet the helper silently maps them to 0.

Triggering scenario: caller passes well-formed leaf + 2 SCTs + a corrupted issuer cert. Current behavior: Ok(0), indistinguishable from 'SCTs are from untrusted logs.' Caller has no way to tell their input was bad.

The docstring (verify.rs:359) explicitly enumerates which failures fold into 0: 'wrong signature, unknown log, retired log, unsupported algorithm.' It does NOT list ParseError or CertDerTooLong. Behavior diverges from documentation.

Suggested fix: short-circuit the per-SCT loop with these two error variants surfacing as errors from verify_embedded_scts, OR document them as folded-into-0. Either way the docstring and behavior must agree.
title: verify_embedded_scts swallows hard input errors (malformed issuer cert) as Ok(0)
